excerpt: Data Journalism Bootcamp FAQ Upcoming Bootcamps: August 2026: - Advanced Data Journalism Bootcamp in Python (in-person) - Registration opening soon - No Python experience required, but some prior experience working with data is recommended - Fellowship applications are open now! - Current IRE membership is required - Aug. 3-7, Columbia, MO What is “bootcamp”? IRE’s Data Journalism Bootcamp is a weeklong, in-person workshop that gives journalists a solid foundation for using data in the newsroom. We cover finding and negotiating for data; vetting, cleaning and analyzing data; and ensuring that your analysis is solid. We call it “bootcamp” because it is intense training that will change your (journalist) life! What's the difference between the three bootcamps? Other than when they take place, each bootcamp offers a different advanced skill toward the end of bootcamp. But all three bootcamps offer the foundational basics: Finding and negotiating for data, vetting your analysis and using numbers in your stories. All three bootcamps ensure that attendees are comfortable working with data in spreadsheets, which is an important skill for every journalist using data in their reporting. No matter which bootcamp you take, you will get intensive training in data fundamentals. What does bootcamp schedule look like? In general, our bootcamps run from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. CT, Monday through Thursday, and from 9 a.m. to noon on Friday. The schedule provides attendees with several breaks and an hour and a half for lunch. We also include three optional open lab sessions after training and two optional group dinners. Schedule for March Bootcamp: Google Sheets deep dive + AI for reporting Day 1: - Introduction to data journalism and examples of reporting using AI - Sorting and formulas in Google Sheets - Ethical and practical considerations of using AI tools - Using Claude to assist in filtering + extracting information from Google Sheets Day 2: - How to find and negotiate for data, FOIA strategies - Using Google Pinpoint to find stories in public records and build databases - Pivot tables - Avoiding errors when working with AI tools Day 3: - Making the data story ironclad / Fact-checking - Getting data out of PDFs - Scraping without coding - Advanced scraping, with coding assist from LLM tools - Building your own database with Gemini and sets of documents in Google Drive - Joining tables in Sheets (XLOOKUP) Day 4: - Numeracy: using numbers in your stories - Cleaning and reformatting your data - Cleaning with OpenRefine - Even more AI tools Day 5: Half day (10am to 12 noon) - Quick Hit Investigations: stories to do at home - IRE resources and benefits (Detailed schedule for August bootcamp coming soon) If I already attended bootcamp, do I need to attend again in the new format? Not necessarily. A lot of the material will be the same as previous bootcamps. If you’ve taken bootcamp already and feel comfortable with spreadsheets and SQL, but want to get into Python, you might consider taking our mini-bootcamp
